data.long_meaning: Deepani is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘deepa’ (light) and ‘ani’ (radiant). This name is associated with wisdom, knowledge, and illumination. It is believed that those named Deepani possess inner light, which guides them through life. The name Deepani carries the meaning “Light, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Deepani usually hope their child will grow to embody light, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Deepani is the name of a queen in the Indian epic Mahabharata. She was the wife of King Virata of Matsya Kingdom and was known for her exceptional beauty and kindness. During the exile of the Pandava brothers, they disguised themselves as servants in Virata's kingdom. Deepani mistook Bhima in disguise for the mighty Bhima and offered him her own bed. Bhima, however, declined her offer and slept on a bed of kusha grass. Impressed by his humility, Deepani was won over by Bhima and they became friends.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that narrates the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and Kaurava princes.

historical_references.reference: Deepani is also the name of a Hindu goddess, particularly worshipped in the Madhya Pradesh region of India. She is believed to be a form of the goddess Parvati and is worshipped for her blessings on child marriage and married life. Deepani Puja is celebrated on the 13th day of the Hindu calendar month of Chaitra (March–April).
historical_references.context: Deepani is a local Hindu goddess revered in certain regions of India for her blessings on married life and child marriages.
